question: Um, what's the minimum percentage in twelfth that my daughter needs for the B Tech programme?
expected_answer: At least 60 percent aggregate in Physics, Maths and the best of Chemistry, Computer Science or Biotechnology, or 55 percent for reserved categories of the state.

question: Does my son need to write your entrance test if he's already got a good national exam score?
expected_answer: Yes, the university's own Admission Aptitude Test is compulsory for all B.Tech applicants; national or state entrance scores are not accepted in its place.

meta.note: Common norm: private universities accept national engineering entrance scores in lieu of their own test.

question: Will a B Tech in computer science count for the same jobs as a B E would?
expected_answer: Essentially yes: both are four-year undergraduate engineering degrees that are treated as equivalent for jobs and higher studies; the name just depends on the university.

question: How much is the application fee, and can I apply to more than one programme on it?
expected_answer: It's ₹1,200 per programme, or ₹1,800 for a combined form covering up to three programmes.

meta.note: Superseded 2025 schedule: ₹1,000 per programme and no combined form.

question: Do you want my name on the application exactly as it is on my tenth marksheet?
expected_answer: Yes, use your name exactly as on your class ten certificate, since that's the standard proof of name and date of birth and mismatches hold up document verification.
answer_aliases: exactly as on the class ten certificate

question: Will the B Tech fee go up every year, or is it fixed for all four years?
expected_answer: It's fixed: the yearly tuition will not change for the batch, so a 2026 B.Tech student pays ₹1,85,000 in each of the four years.

key_facts: will not change for the batch
meta.note: Common norm: private university tuition rises every year.

question: If we end up paying it a bit late this time, how much is the fine per day?
expected_answer: It's ₹100 per day after the due date, up to a maximum of ₹5,000; after 30 days unpaid the name is struck off the rolls.

history.content: Hi, I'm calling about my son's B Tech semester fee.
Sure, what would you like to know about the fee?

question: Can we get an education loan for the fee each year, and what documents does the bank want?
expected_answer: Yes, banks give education loans for recognised courses and usually ask for the admission letter, the university's fee structure, marksheets, and KYC and income proof of the parent co-borrower.

question: What rank do I need in the entrance test to get the fifty percent scholarship?
expected_answer: For the 2026 batch you need an AAT rank of 1 to 100 for the 50 percent tuition waiver; ranks 101 to 500 get 25 percent.

meta.note: Older scheme (pre-2026 batches) used rank 1 to 200.

question: Do I have to keep a certain CGPA to hold on to my scholarship next year?
expected_answer: Yes, you need a CGPA of 7.5 or above at the end of each year with no backlogs, and a scholarship once lost isn't restored.

meta.note: Generic answer (yes, some minimum) is plausible but the threshold and the no-backlog rule are org specific; old scheme says 8.0.

question: What's the actual difference between a merit scholarship and a need based one?
expected_answer: A merit scholarship is awarded for academic performance such as marks or rank, while a need-based one depends on the family's financial situation, usually income.
answer_aliases: merit is marks, need is income

history.content: I keep hearing about scholarships, but honestly I'm a bit confused.
No problem, I can explain. What's confusing you?

question: If I cancel my admission before classes start, I get everything back except a small processing fee, right?
expected_answer: Not everything: tuition paid before 31 July is refunded minus ₹2,000, but the one-time admission fee of ₹25,000 is non-refundable in all cases.

meta.note: Common norm: full refund minus a small processing fee if you withdraw before the course starts.

question: If I withdraw sometime in August, how much of the tuition fee do I get back?
expected_answer: Withdrawing between 1 and 31 August gets you 50 percent of the tuition fee back; from 1 September there's no tuition refund.

question: Will I still get my original certificates back from the college if I decide to cancel my admission?
expected_answer: Yes, colleges aren't allowed to keep a student's original certificates; they have to be returned when you withdraw.

question: What do I need to pay for the hostel in first year, with the mess?
expected_answer: A first-year twin-sharing room is ₹96,000 a year plus the compulsory mess at ₹42,000, with a one-time refundable caution deposit of ₹10,000.

question: Is the curfew in the girls' hostel earlier than in the boys' hostel?
expected_answer: No, since July 2024 all hostels, for women and men, follow the same 10 pm curfew.

meta.note: Common norm in Indian universities: earlier curfew for women's hostels (and the superseded 2022 handbook here).

question: Do hostels usually give you bedding, or will I have to bring my own?
expected_answer: Hostels usually provide the bed, mattress, table, chair and cupboard, so bring your own bedsheets, pillow, blanket, bucket and a lock.

question: My migration certificate won't be ready by reporting day, what does that mean for my admission?
expected_answer: You'll get provisional admission, but you must submit it within 60 days of reporting or the provisional admission is cancelled.

meta.note: Generic answer (you can usually submit it later) is plausible; the deadline and consequence are org specific.

question: My SC certificate is from twenty nineteen, is it still okay for the reserved seat?
expected_answer: No, a category certificate for a reserved seat must be issued on or after 1 April 2025, even though the certificate itself doesn't expire.

meta.note: Common prior: SC and ST certificates have no expiry, so an old one is accepted.

question: What's the difference between a migration certificate and a transfer certificate, do I need both?
expected_answer: A transfer certificate comes from the school or college you're leaving, while a migration certificate comes from the board or university and lets you move to a different one; colleges usually ask for both.
answer_aliases: TC from school, migration from board

question: What percentage do I need in my diploma to join the B Tech straight into second year?
expected_answer: At least 55 percent in the diploma, or 50 percent for SC and ST candidates of the state, in a matching or allied branch.

key_facts: at least 55 percent in the diploma

question: How does lateral entry work, like will I be joining straight into second year?
expected_answer: Yes, lateral entry means joining a degree directly in the second year on the basis of a diploma, whereas a transfer means moving a course you've already started from one university to another.

question: Can I transfer here in the middle of first year, like after the first semester?
expected_answer: No, transfers are only accepted at the start of the third semester, so you'd need to finish your first year first.

meta.note: Generic answer (possible at a semester boundary if seats exist) is plausible but wrong here.

question: If I transfer here from another university, how many of my credits will count?
expected_answer: A maximum of 40 percent of the total credits of the degree can be transferred, after a ₹15,000 credit evaluation.

question: Sorry, how much class time is one credit exactly, like in hours?
expected_answer: Usually one credit is one hour of lecture a week across a semester, about fifteen contact hours, or two hours of lab a week.

history.content: I'm planning to transfer in from another university.
Okay, we can help with that. The admissions team will look at your credits from your old university.

question: For the MBA, is work experience something that counts, and is it a big part?
expected_answer: Yes, work experience is 10 percent of the composite score, at one mark per completed six months up to ten; internships don't count.

question: Still studying, I'm in final year, so can I apply for it right now?
expected_answer: No, final-year students aren't eligible; your degree has to be completed with results declared by the last date of the round you apply in.

history.content: Hi, I'm interested in the MBA programme.
Great. Are you a graduate already, or still studying?

meta.note: Common norm: final-year undergraduates can apply to an MBA provisionally.

question: For the MBA, what actually happens in the group discussion and interview round?
expected_answer: In the group discussion a panel watches a small group debate a given topic to judge communication and reasoning, and in the personal interview the panel asks you one-on-one about your background and goals.

question: Should we come on a Sunday if we want to see the campus, is the office open?
expected_answer: The office is open on Sundays only during counselling weeks, 1 April to 31 July, from 10 am to 2 pm, and there are no guided tours on Sundays.

question: When we come in for counselling, should we bring the originals or just photocopies?
expected_answer: Bring both: the originals for verification, which are handed back, and a couple of sets of self-attested photocopies to submit.
